# The 7-gate understandability checklist (plan.md §5.5, §6.15)

Applied **per company, against that company's own evidence — never as a
verdict on its sector** (plan.md §5.2). A cyclical is not failed merely for
being cyclical, nor a bank for having a balance sheet; the question is
always "can *this* business, on *this* evidence, be explained and
underwritten."

1. **`five_sentence_business_model`** — can you state, in five sentences or
   fewer, what the company does, to whom, and how it makes money? If you
   need a sixth sentence, the test fails — that is itself informative, not
   a formatting nuisance.
2. **`unit_economics_clarity`** — can you trace how one unit of the
   business's core activity (one loan, one policy, one tonne of output, one
   subscriber) turns into profit? If the unit economics are opaque even
   after reading the filings, this fails.
3. **`industry_structure_stability`** — is the industry's structure (who
   the competitors are, how they compete, what determines pricing power)
   stable enough to reason about 5-10 years out? A fast-consolidating or
   technologically-disrupted industry can still pass if you can name *why*
   the structure is nonetheless predictable; otherwise it fails.
4. **`demand_forecastability_5_10yr`** — can you make a reasoned case for
   demand 5-10 years out, distinct from industry structure (this is about
   the *product*, not the *competitors*)? A commodity with fully cyclical,
   unpredictable demand fails this even if the industry structure itself
   (gate 3) is stable.
5. **`management_understandability`** — can you characterize management's
   capital-allocation track record and communication style from cited
   evidence (concalls, annual report letters, capex decisions)? "Cannot
   tell what management actually does with capital" fails this gate.
6. **`accounting_transparency`** — are the financial statements legible: no
   unexplained related-party structures, no serial one-off "exceptional
   items," no auditor qualifications you cannot explain? A cited accounting
   red flag fails this gate, distinct from the Integrity Gate (§18), which
   is about promoter conduct rather than statement legibility.
7. **`identifiable_moat_source`** — can you name the *specific* source of
   any competitive advantage (brand, switching cost, network effect, cost
   advantage, efficient scale/regulatory) with evidence, not just assert
   "the company has a moat"? "No identifiable source" is itself a valid,
   honest answer that fails this gate.

**All seven must pass for the gate to pass.** A single failed gate fails
dossier §15 as a whole — record the failure as "not underwritable on the
available evidence," name the specific gate that failed, and state what
evidence would resolve it (plan.md §5.5).
